instructions: Complete the summary below. Write ONE WORD AND/OR A NUMBER for each answer.
stem_block:
HOW THE PLASTIC MOVES, AND HOW IT IS COUNTED

A fragment reaching the sea floats to begin with. Sunlight and the movement of the water leave the polymer brittle enough to break apart, and living organisms then form a coating over each piece — the lecturer's name for this is (36) ......... The added weight takes the particle downwards; in colder water the coating is grazed off, the particle lifts again, and a great deal of the material is therefore oscillating rather than lying still on the bottom.

Samples at the surface are taken with a manta trawl pulled along beside a boat. Two such studies can be set against each other only when both of them report the (37) ........ size of the net, and a great many papers never do. Dated cores give a cleaner record: the first plastic particles turn up in sediment from the (38) ........, and the amount has roughly doubled every fifteen years since. On beaches, where the counting is largely done by volunteers, ten kinds of product make up some three quarters of what is recorded, and (39) ........, which escape during transport rather than being thrown away, are listed on their own in almost every survey.

Four responses are ranked: better design, extended producer responsibility, interception in rivers — of limited use, since booms work only in low flow — and, most valuable of all, (40) ........ the monitoring, so that size classes and reporting units are agreed.

items.prompt: living organisms then form a coating over each piece — the lecturer's name for this is (36) ........
items.explanation: The layer that living organisms form on the surface of a broken fragment is called biofouling; it is this layer that weighs the particle down and sinks it.

items.prompt: Two such studies can be set against each other only when both of them report the (37) ........ size of the net
items.evidence: you cannot put two studies side by side unless you know the mesh each of them used
items.explanation: The finer the mesh, the more particles are counted per cubic metre; that is why two studies that don't report their mesh size cannot be compared.

items.prompt: the first plastic particles turn up in sediment from the (38) ........
items.evidence: show plastic particles appearing first in layers laid down in the nineteen fifties
items.explanation: In dated cores taken from sheltered basins, plastic first appears in layers from the 1950s; the amount has roughly doubled every fifteen years since then.

items.prompt: and (39) ........, which escape during transport rather than being thrown away, are listed on their own in almost every survey
items.evidence: The other category worth naming is pellets — the raw granules that are melted down to make everything else.
items.explanation: Pellets are the raw granules that everything else is melted down from; since they are lost during transport rather than thrown away, they are counted as a separate category.

items.prompt: and, most valuable of all, (40) ........ the monitoring, so that size classes and reporting units are agreed
items.evidence: And fourth — least photogenic, most useful — standardising the monitoring.
items.explanation: The fourth step, and according to the lecturer the most useful one, is standardising the monitoring; half the debate in the field is about arithmetic rather than the ocean.
